title: Difference equation
summary: Linear recurrence of order 2 with constant coefficients.

methods.name: Characteristic equation
methods.reason: The recurrence is linear with constant coefficients, so it is solved like a constant-coefficient differential equation with \(r^n\) in place of \(e^{rx}\).

steps.title: Write the characteristic equation
steps.text: Try \(a_n = r^n\) in the homogeneous recurrence (right-hand side 0) and divide by \(r^n\). This is the same idea as trying \(e^{rx}\) in a differential equation with constant coefficients.

steps.title: Homogeneous solution
steps.text: Combine the solutions with arbitrary constants.

steps.title: Write the general solution
steps.text: With right-hand side 0 this is the whole solution.

steps.title: Apply the starting values
steps.text: Set \(n = 0, 1\) and solve for the constants.

steps.title: First terms
steps.text: From the formula; they agree with stepping the recurrence forward.

steps.title: Long-run behaviour
steps.text: A root has \(|r| > 1\), so solutions generally grow without bound, like \(|r|^n\) with \(|r| = 1.61803\).

steps.title: Check
steps.text: The formula reproduces the first 30 terms computed directly from the recurrence.

methods.name: Direct iteration
methods.reason: Starting values are given, so the terms can be computed one after another. This gives numbers but no formula for \(a_n\).
